author: reek
body: Adversarial probe for the mask query builtins, and the pin for the movmskpd REX omission.

author: reek
body: Two things are needed to reach it, and every existing vector test in the tree has neither. The operands must have DISTINCT LANES, because vec-splat writes the same value to both and movmskpd can then only answer 0 or 3 -- under which mask-any and mask-all are the same function and mask-count is never asked for 1. And several queries must sit in ONE arithmetic expression, because which temp a query is handed depends on how many the surrounding expression has already consumed. mk2 builds a distinct-lane vector by writing two doubles into a buffer, which is the only way to express one.

author: reek
body: The lane-uniform variants are the controls: they answer correctly even on a compiler carrying the defect, which is precisely why splat-only tests could not see it.

author: reek
body: An empty mask: every lane clear, so none is True and any and all are False.

author: reek
body: A mixed mask: lane zero set, lane one clear. This is the pattern vec-splat cannot produce, and the only one under which count is 1.

author: reek
body: Lane-uniform operands. These answer correctly with or without the fix, so a run where these pass and the probes above fail is the signature of the defect rather than of vectors being broken generally.
